newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 10.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Leader of the Democratic United National Lalith Front (DUNLF) Srimani Athulathmudali says the decision by President Chandrika Kumaratunga to sack her from the cabinet of ministers is a breach of contract. Kumaratunga's Sri Lanka Freedom Party (SLFP) signed an agreeement with DUNLF promising its leader a cabinet portfolio in exchange for support during the 1994 general election.
Kumaratunga names eight new cabinet ministers and 11 deputy ministers in cabinet reshuffle, increasing the nubmer of ministers to 30 and deputy ministers to 33.

Kumaratunga says new ministers and deputy ministers will not be entitled to additional funds, new office buildings, more staff and vehicles and that they will have to make do with existing facilities.
Senior minister Dharmasiri Senanayake loses media ministry, which was given to Posts and Telecommunications Minister Mangala Samaraweera.
Troops on Operation Jaya Sikuru or Sure of Victory consolidate in Periyamadu, a village just south of the fortified rebel-held northern town of Puliyankulam, defence sources say.
